_doc: PRIOR ART: scripts/lib/ocr-routing-table.json (the OCR side, by page kind, #6688; its `route` fields are read by ocr-routing.mjs since #7170). Before #7170 the translation policy lived only as two regexes in scripts/lib/translate-core.mjs and their TS twin in src/lib/types/ai-models.ts. This file is that policy, READ by both routers (getTranslateModelForBook): the first row whose `match` fits the book gives the engine, else `default`. A `language_prefix` matches the FIRST language label, case-insensitively, as a whole word, with any run of spaces for a space ("greek" matches "Greek, Latin" and not "Latin; Greek"); `optional_lead` words may stand before any prefix ("Ancient Hebrew"). A row is `channel: "batch"` (the default) or `channel: "cli"` (#7075). A batch row names one of the two Batch models (gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3-flash-preview). A cli row names a subscription reader (CLI_TRANSLATE_LANES in translation-routing.mjs: claude-opus-5-5, gemini-3.8-flash+agy-cli), carries `adoption` (the blind sample against the reader it replaces) and OVERLAYS the batch rows: the Batch routers never see it, and the pipeline orchestrator holds its books (CLI_TRANSLATE_HOLD) for scripts/batch/cli-translate-lane.mjs. Any other engine or channel fails the test. Changes are proposed by scripts/eval/estimator/routing/derive_routes.py and land as a reviewed edit of this file with the evidence that justifies them. tests/unit/translate-core-parity.test.ts pins the two routers to each other and to this file.

default.why: #4759: translation reads text, not images; the only A/B on record (#467) favoured lite and the observational read of the lite era found no faithfulness gap.
